steps.title: Import Vue and createApp
steps.instruction: Import Vue and createApp from 'vue' to initialize the Vue application.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary Vue functions.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing functions from a library
import { createApp } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the Vue functions imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Vue and createApp are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and createApp.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and createApp from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import Vue and createApp from 'vue'.

steps.title: Import Zustand and persist middleware
steps.instruction: Import the 'create' function from 'zustand' and the 'persist' middleware from 'zustand/middleware'.
steps.hint: You'll need two import statements: one for the main Zustand function and one for the middleware.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing functions from different modules
import { createApp } from 'vue'
import { create } from 'zustand'
import { persist } from 'zustand/middleware'
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and createApp here
import { createApp } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports for Zustand and its persist middleware are added to the file.
successCriteria: The 'create' function is imported from 'zustand' and the 'persist' middleware is imported from 'zustand/middleware'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Zustand and the persist middleware.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both 'create' from 'zustand' and 'persist' from 'zustand/middleware'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import the Zustand library and its persist middleware.

steps.title: Create the Vue app instance
steps.instruction: Create a Vue app instance using createApp() and assign it to a variable named 'app'.
steps.hint: Call createApp() and store the result in a variable called 'app'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating an app instance
const app = createApp()
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue app instance is created and ready to be configured.
successCriteria: A variable named 'app' is declared and assigned the result of createApp().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Vue app instance.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling createApp() and storing it in a variable named 'app'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Vue app instance wasn't created correctly. You need to call createApp() and assign it to a variable named 'app'.

steps.title: Define the Zustand store with initial state
steps.instruction: Define a Zustand store using create() with an initial state object containing a count property set to 0. Name the store useCountStore.
steps.hint: Call create() from zustand and pass it a function that returns an object with a count property initialized to 0.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Zustand store named useCountStore is defined with an initial state containing count: 0.
successCriteria: The store is defined using create() and returns an object with a count property set to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined a Zustand store with initial state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using create() and defining count: 0 in the state object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store definition is missing or incorrect. Use create() to define a store with count: 0.

steps.title: Add persist middleware to the store
steps.instruction: Wrap your existing store definition with the persist middleware, providing a name for localStorage (e.g., 'counter-store').
steps.hint: Use the persist middleware you imported earlier to wrap your store creation. The persist function takes the store configuration and an options object with a name property.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your store will be wrapped with the persist middleware, enabling automatic persistence to localStorage with the specified name.
successCriteria: The store is wrapped with persist middleware and includes a name property in the options object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the persist middleware to your store. This will automatically save your state to localStorage.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're wrapping the entire store configuration with persist() and providing a name property in the options object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Remember to wrap your store definition with persist() and include a name property for localStorage.

steps.title: Define store actions
steps.instruction: Add a reset action to your Zustand store that sets the count back to 0.
steps.hint: Inside the create function, add another property to the object alongside increment. The reset action should call set with { count: 0 }.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store will have a reset action that can be called to reset the count to 0.
successCriteria: The useStore definition includes a reset action that calls set with { count: 0 }.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a reset action to your store. Now you have both increment and reset actions to modify the count state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're adding the reset action inside the same create function, and it should call set with { count: 0 }.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reset action wasn't added correctly. Check that you're adding it as a property in the same object as increment, and it should call set with { count: 0 }.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'App' using the <script setup> syntax. The component should have a template section with a root <div> element.
steps.hint: Use the <script setup> syntax to define a Vue component. Start with a <template> section containing a <div> as the root element.
steps.analogousExample: // Example of a basic Vue component
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named 'App' is created with <script setup> and a template containing a root <div> element.
successCriteria: The component is named 'App', uses <script setup> syntax, and has a template with a root <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main Vue component structure. This gives us a foundation to build our persistent counter interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've included all required elements: component named 'App', <script setup> syntax, and a template with a root <div>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Remember to create a Vue component named 'App' with <script setup> and a template containing a root <div> element.

steps.title: Use the store in the component
steps.instruction: In your Vue component, import the Zustand store and access the count state to display it in the template.
steps.hint: Use the useStore hook you created earlier to get the count value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Accessing store state in a Vue component
const count = useStore((state) => state.count)
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will be able to read the count state from the Zustand store.
successCriteria: The component imports and uses the useStore hook to access the count state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully connected your Vue component to the Zustand store.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing the store and accessing the count state correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't properly accessing the store state. Check that you're importing useStore and calling it to get the count.

steps.title: Display the count state
steps.instruction: In your Vue component's template, add a paragraph element that displays the current count value from the store.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to output the count value from the store in your template.
steps.analogousExample: // Displaying a value in Vue template
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will show the current count value in a paragraph element.
successCriteria: Paragraph displays count value using {{ }} syntax
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the persisted count state in your Vue component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct syntax to output the count value in the paragraph.
steps.feedbackWrong: The count value isn't being displayed correctly. Check that you're using the store's count property with the correct template syntax.

steps.title: Add buttons and wire store actions
steps.instruction: Add a button element to the template that calls the increment action when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to call the increment method from your store.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Similar: button that triggers a store action -->
<button @click="store.increment">Increment</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Increment' appears in the UI that increases the count when clicked.
successCriteria: The template contains a button element with @click="store.increment" that triggers the increment action.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that calls the increment action from your Zustand store.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it uses @click to call the store's increment method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly wired to the store action. Check that you're using @click with the correct store method.
